problem: Classical offline-trained AI models struggle to adapt to dynamic, unstructured environments, and the literature on embodied intelligence is fragmented between early navigation-centric tasks and newer LLM/MLM-based robot schemes.
motivation: Embodied intelligence, which learns through interaction with the environment, is seen as a route to AGI. As LLMs and multimodal large models (MLMs) are integrated with robots, a unified view of tasks, models and system schemes is needed to organize the field and guide future work.
key_idea: A survey that reviews early embodied tasks, categorizes LLM/MLM-based robot embodied intelligence schemes, and summarizes them under a perception-planning-action (PPA) paradigm.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations or analysis can be cited. The abstract states that the PPA paradigm unifies the various LLM/MLM-based schemes, and that LLM/MLM prior knowledge enables reasoning and planning for more complex tasks than early navigation.
method: Early embodied tasks review: surveys initial embodied tasks (primarily navigation) and the corresponding research.
Scheme categorization: classifies current LLM/MLM-based embodied intelligence schemes deployed on robots.
PPA paradigm: summarizes the perception-planning-action paradigm shared across these schemes.
Performance evaluation: evaluates the performance of MLMs across the different schemes.
Future directions: offers insights on future development in the field.
numbers_note: abstract only; survey with no method results extracted
results: The abstract reports no quantitative results. It says the survey evaluates MLM performance across schemes and identifies future directions.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so the details of the taxonomy and evaluation cannot be assessed.
As a survey, it presents no new method or benchmark results.
